tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: Use this when someone asks which Croncool projects they have, or a project's id is needed. Returns each project's id, name and creation time, 50 by default and 100 at most, with a flag when more exist. Not for listing jobs.

tools.name: list_jobs
tools.description: Use this when someone asks what cron jobs or scheduled tasks they have, or which ones last failed. Returns each job's id, name, schedule, target origin, method, enabled state and last run status and time, 20 per page by default, with a cursor for more. Not for a job's full run history.

tools.name: get_job
tools.description: Use this when someone asks about one cron job's schedule or target, or whether it is enabled and last succeeded. Returns the job's name, cron expression, type, target origin, HTTP method, content type, enabled state and last run status and time, or not-found. Not for running the job.

tools.name: run_job
tools.description: Use this when someone asks to run or trigger a cron job now. Returns only that Croncool invoked it, not the target's response. Each call immediately sends the job's configured request again, which can write, message or bill downstream, and a repeated call sends it once more. Not for checking a run's

tools.name: get_job_runs
tools.description: Use this when someone asks whether a cron job ran, failed or was slow, including a run just triggered. Returns recent runs newest first with success or failure, HTTP status, duration and time (no response bodies), 20 by default and 100 at most. Not for starting a run.

tools.name: list_workflows
tools.description: Use this when someone asks which durable workflows a Croncool project runs, or how many runs are running, pending, completed, failed or cancelled. Returns each workflow's name, run counts by status and last run time for one project, 50 by default and 100 at most. Not for individual runs.

tools.name: list_workflow_runs
tools.description: Use this when someone asks about recent or failed runs of a durable workflow in a Croncool project. Returns each run's id, workflow name, status, timings and error code, newest first by default, 20 per page with a cursor, filterable by workflow and status. Not for one run's steps.

tools.name: get_workflow_run
tools.description: Use this when someone asks why a durable workflow run failed or where it is stuck. Returns the run's status, timings and error code plus its steps with status, attempt, timings and error code, 50 steps by default and 200 at most. Not for listing runs.

tools.name: list_webhook_subscriptions
tools.description: Use this when someone asks whether their Croncool webhooks are delivering, failing or were disabled. Returns each subscription's endpoint origin, events, active state, consecutive failures, auto-disabled flag and last delivery time, 20 by default. Works only with a signed-in user session, not an API

tools.name: open_croncool
tools.description: Use this when someone wants to open Croncool and browse their projects and scheduled jobs, with schedules, target origins and latest run status, in an interactive sidebar. Returns up to 100 projects to start from (no request payloads, workflow bodies, secrets or full target URLs). Not for running jo

tools.name: show_project_overview
tools.description: Use this when someone wants a quick overview or dashboard of one Croncool project. Returns an overview card with the project's name and creation time, whether workflow hosting is set up, and up to 12 jobs with schedule, target origin and last run status. Not for a job's run history.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "open_croncool" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: open_croncool · Private data: list_webhook_subscriptions, open_croncool · Public sink: list_webhook_subscriptions · Destructive: list_jobs, get_job, run_job, get_job_runs, list_workflows, list_workflow_runs, get_workflow_run, open_croncool, show_project_overview.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: open_croncool · Private data: list_webhook_subscriptions, open_croncool · Public sink: list_webhook_subscriptions · Destructive: list_jobs, get_job, run_job, get_job_runs, list_workflows, list_workflow_runs, get_workflow_run, open_croncool, show_project_overview

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "list_projects" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "List a bounded set of Croncool projects the authenticated user can access. Returns only the project id needed for follow-up calls, display name, and creation time; workflow callback configuration and secrets are excluded." → after: "Use this when someone asks which Croncool projects they have, or a project's id is needed. Returns each project's id, name and creation time, 50 by default and 100 at most, with a flag when more exist. Not for listing jobs."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
